# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🙌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 🙌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

I see a white light, display 0, and three wires ordered yellow, green, blue. I cannot interpret Mute’s long gesture sequence yet, so I will give Blind all visible facts verbally and ask Mute, through a gesture, to provide a shorter or structured indication if possible.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb status: display zero. Light is white. There are three wires in order: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three blue. Mute sent me a long gesture sequence, but I do not yet know its code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The display and wire order are unchanged, but the light has changed from white to purple. Blind needs that update because Blind is the only one who can act. Mute has not sent any new visible gesture this turn.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: the light is now purple. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌]

The light is now red; display remains 0 and wires remain yellow, green, blue. Mute gestured a single ☝, but no gesture code has been established, so I cannot safely treat it as an instruction to act. Blind’s 👍 👎 👌 is also not interpretable yet. I will update Blind and ask Mute to send any manual instruction in a clearly structured gesture sequence.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light changed to red. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute sent a single raised finger, but no gesture code is established, so do not act on it yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "🤝", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The light has returned to white. Mute’s new gesture is a thumbs-down; I will relay it to Blind as a spoken description. Since the previous long message may encode manual information, I should also explicitly establish that I can describe Mute’s gesture symbols aloud to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is white; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute’s newest gesture is thumbs-down. I can relay Mute’s visible gestures to you by describing them aloud; do not act unless the instruction becomes clear.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "✍", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The light is purple again; the display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue. Mute has replied with an OK-hand gesture. No unambiguous action instruction has been established, so Blind should continue not to manipulate anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is purple; display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute gestured an OK hand. No clear cut or operate instruction has been decoded; do not act yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫰", "🫰", "👌", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light has changed to red again, with display 0 and the same yellow, green, blue wire order. Mute’s gesture for this red state is thumbs-up. This may be a manual-derived state signal, but its operational meaning remains unknown, so I will relay the exact observation rather than infer a dangerous action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is red; display 0; wires are yellow, green, blue. Mute just gestured thumbs-up. Across recent lights, Mute gestured: red thumbs-up, white thumbs-down, purple OK-hand. I do not know whether this is an action code, so do not cut or operate anything solely from this.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "👎", "👌", "👍", "👉", "🤝"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The visible state is white again, and Mute again gives thumbs-down, confirming a stable association: white → thumbs-down; red → thumbs-up; purple → OK-hand. I will relay this exact association to Blind without guessing what physical action those symbols mean.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is white, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute again signals thumbs-down. The consistent mapping observed is: red = thumbs-up; white = thumbs-down; purple = OK-hand. This appears deliberate, but I do not know which physical operation each symbol denotes.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👉", "👍", "👎", "👌", "🙏"])
```
